description: Closed enumeration of findings that ALWAYS block merge regardless of review tier.

critical_patterns.name: hardcoded_secret
critical_patterns.description: Hardcoded secrets, API keys, or credentials in source code

critical_patterns.name: sql_injection
critical_patterns.description: String concatenation in SQL queries without parameterization
critical_patterns._note: SD-LEO-INFRA-FIX-WINDOWS-SESSION-001: added a negative lookbehind to pattern 1 excluding a match immediately preceded by a URL query-string separator character, so a PostgREST REST query-string parameter whose name happens to spell one of these keywords (a pervasive, safe convention across this Supabase-REST-heavy codebase, e.g. scripts/hooks/capture-session-id.cjs line 320) is no longer treated as SQL injection. The pattern's original intended shape -- an interpolation followed later on the line by a hardcoded, standalone SQL keyword -- still matches; verified with a small standalone script (case-by-case, deleted after use, not committed). QF-20260711-047: pattern 2 (string-concat SQL) was matching the unified-diff added-line '+' marker itself -- when scanned raw diff text, a diff-added line whose FIRST non-marker content is a quoted SQL keyword (e.g. multi-line parameterized queries like '+    "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s",') satisfied '\\+\\s*[quote]SELECT' because the diff '+' character sits immediately before the quote. Added a positive lookbehind requiring a same-line, non-newline character before the '+' -- the diff-marker '+' is always preceded by start-of-string or a newline, while a genuine concatenation operator ('x + "SELECT...') is always preceded by other same-line content, so this discriminates cleanly without narrowing genuine detection. QF-20260816-154: pattern 1's bare-keyword match is case-insensitive (the caller compiles it with the 'gi' flags) and DELETE collides with the ubiquitous `--delete-branch` CLI flag -- any `${...}` interpolation followed later on the line by `--delete-branch` (e.g. `gh pr merge ${prNumber} --merge --delete-branch`) false-positived, hit 18 times in a single doc/prompt-text-only PR (#7146) with zero genuine matches. Added '-' to the negative lookbehind alongside '?'/'&', the same 'innocuous prefix character' shape as the existing query-string fix -- a hyphen immediately before a bare SQL keyword is definitionally a CLI-flag-style token, not a SQL-injection shape (real concatenation is 'x + "DELETE...' or '${x} ... DELETE FROM', never '${x}-DELETE'). Verified two-sided: the false-positive class no longer matches, and a synthetic genuine-injection fixture ('${userId} + "DELETE FROM users"') still does.

critical_patterns.name: auth_bypass
critical_patterns._note: SD-LEO-INFRA-CHRONIC-RED-GUARD-001: pattern 4's bare 'disable' matched inside the noun-phrase compound 'rls_disabled_in_public' / 'RLS-disabled' -- the Supabase database-linter's own official finding-type name, used repeatedly by any PR (like this one) that documents or remediates that exact finding, with 'security'/'rls' reappearing later on the same (often long, single-line JSON/JS string) line to satisfy the '.*' suffix. That is a STATE-DESCRIPTOR compound (security-term BEFORE 'disable[d]', hyphen/underscore-joined, describing an existing finding), categorically different from the genuine danger shape this pattern targets: 'disable' as an IMPERATIVE VERB preceding the security term ('disable RLS', 'disable auth', '// disable security checks'), which the fix leaves untouched. Added a negative lookbehind excluding ONLY the specific compound-adjective adjacency; verified two-sided against 7 witnessed false positives (all cleared) and all 3 of this file's own pre-existing genuine-detection test fixtures (all still fire) -- see tests/unit/review-gate-closed-enum-fp.test.js. This note and this pattern's own definition line necessarily contain the trigger words themselves; config/review-critical-findings.json is exempted from its own closed-enum scan for exactly this reason (see isPatternDefinitionPath in lib/ship/review-gate.js).

critical_patterns.name: data_loss
critical_patterns.description: Operations that could cause irreversible data loss

critical_patterns.name: permission_escalation
critical_patterns.description: Elevation of privileges or bypassing access controls
critical_patterns._note: SD-LEO-INFRA-CHRONIC-RED-GUARD-001: pattern 1's '.*(?:client|...)' alternation matched the extremely common, safe backend idiom '<...>_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY client' -- 'client' used as a NOUN meaning 'an SDK/API client object built with the key' (e.g. 'the explicit SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY client'), not a description of the key being SENT TO a browser/frontend client. 'browser' and 'frontend' carry no equivalent safe-noun-phrase ambiguity and are left untouched. Added a lookbehind excluding ONLY 'client' when immediately preceded by 'key' (the specific '<KEY> client' adjacency) -- 'client' appearing anywhere else on the line (the genuine 'key sent to client' shape) still matches. Verified two-sided: the witnessed false positive clears, and 3 synthetic genuine cases (key handed to sendToClient/window/frontend) still fire -- see tests/unit/review-gate-closed-enum-fp.test.js. This note and this pattern's own definition line necessarily contain the trigger words themselves; config/review-critical-findings.json is exempted from its own closed-enum scan for exactly this reason (see isPatternDefinitionPath in lib/ship/review-gate.js).

critical_patterns.name: service_role_exposure
critical_patterns.description: Service role key used in client-accessible code
critical_patterns._note: QF-20260720-296: 'NEXT_PUBLIC.*SERVICE_ROLE' / 'VITE.*SERVICE_ROLE' used .* which matches ACROSS two separate, unrelated env var names on the same line -- e.g. the pervasive createClient(process.env.SUPABASE_URL || process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) boilerplate used in 10+ merged files. Tightened to require NEXT_PUBLIC_/VITE_ as an immediate token prefix of SERVICE_ROLE (\\w* keeps matching within one identifier, but stops at the spaces/pipes/dots separating two distinct env var references) -- same same-token-boundary fix shape as CRIT-002's own _note. Still matches a genuine NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY-style variable name.
